title: Supplier Onboarding Policy
content:
SUPPLIER ONBOARDING POLICY

Version 4.2 | Procurement Policy Office

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This policy governs the process by which new suppliers are evaluated, approved, and registered in the company's approved supplier list (ASL). It applies to all business units that engage third-party suppliers for goods or services valued above £5,000 per annum. Temporary or one-time purchases below this threshold may use an expedited process described in the Low-Value Procurement Procedure.

2. DEFINITIONS

2.1 Supplier: Any external organisation or individual providing goods, services, or works in exchange for payment.
2.2 Approved Supplier List (ASL): The central register of suppliers who have completed onboarding and are authorised for use.
2.3 Onboarding Lead: The procurement manager responsible for coordinating the onboarding review for a given supplier.
2.4 Risk Tier: A classification (Tier 1–3) assigned during onboarding based on spend, criticality, and risk exposure (see Supplier Risk Tiering Guide).

3. ONBOARDING STAGES

3.1 Initiation
A business unit submits a Supplier Nomination Form (SNF) to the Procurement Policy Office. The form must include the business justification, estimated annual spend, and proposed contract start date. Nominations are reviewed within five working days.

3.2 Sanctions and Compliance Screening
All nominated suppliers must be screened against the company's restricted party list and applicable international sanctions registers before any commercial engagement. See the Sanctions and Restricted Party Screening Policy for procedure. Onboarding is suspended for any supplier that returns a potential match until the Legal and Compliance team issues a written clearance.

3.3 Financial and Legal Due Diligence
The Onboarding Lead requests the following documents from the supplier:
- Certificate of incorporation or equivalent legal registration
- Most recent two years of audited financial statements (or management accounts for SMEs)
- Evidence of relevant insurance coverage (see Insurance and Liability Requirements Policy)
- Data processing agreement or GDPR compliance statement where personal data will be processed
- Quality certification evidence where required by the procuring business unit (see Quality Certification Requirements Policy)

3.4 Risk Tier Assignment
Following receipt of documents, the Onboarding Lead assigns a Risk Tier according to the Supplier Risk Tiering Guide. Tier 1 suppliers require executive sign-off before approval. Tier 2 suppliers require Head of Procurement sign-off. Tier 3 suppliers may be approved by the Onboarding Lead.

3.5 ASL Registration
Approved suppliers are added to the ASL within two working days of final sign-off. The entry includes the supplier's name, registration number, primary contact, approved categories, risk tier, and the next scheduled review date.

4. ONGOING OBLIGATIONS

Suppliers must notify the company within 10 business days of any material change to their legal status, ownership, or financial position. Failure to do so may result in suspension from the ASL pending re-evaluation.

5. REVIEW CYCLE

Tier 1 suppliers are reviewed annually. Tier 2 suppliers are reviewed every two years. Tier 3 suppliers are reviewed every three years, or upon contract renewal, whichever is sooner.

6. NON-COMPLIANCE

Engaging a supplier not on the ASL without prior written exemption from the Head of Procurement constitutes a policy violation and may result in disciplinary action. The relevant business unit head will be notified of any violations.

title: Supplier Payment Terms Policy
content:
SUPPLIER PAYMENT TERMS POLICY

Version 2.1 | Finance & Procurement

1. PURPOSE

This policy establishes the standard payment terms and conditions applicable to all supplier invoices raised against the company. It is intended to ensure consistency, support cash-flow planning, and maintain compliance with the Late Payment of Commercial Debts legislation.

2. STANDARD PAYMENT TERMS

2.1 The company's standard payment term is net 30 days from the date a valid invoice is received and approved in the purchase-to-pay system. This applies to all new supplier agreements unless an exception is approved in writing by the CFO or their delegate.

2.2 For contracts with certified SMEs (as defined by Companies Act 2006 criteria at the time of contract award), a net 20 day term applies. The company is a signatory to the Prompt Payment Code and commits to honoring these obligations.

2.3 Strategic or critical suppliers designated as Tier 1 in the Supplier Risk Tiering Guide may negotiate bespoke payment terms during contract formation. Any term shorter than net 15 days or longer than net 60 days requires approval from the Chief Financial Officer.

3. INVOICE REQUIREMENTS

For an invoice to be considered valid and initiate the payment clock, it must include:
- The company's legal entity name and registered address
- A valid purchase order (PO) number issued by the procurement system
- An itemised description of goods or services delivered
- The relevant delivery address or service period
- The supplier's bank account details (IBAN/SWIFT for international payments)
- VAT number and VAT breakdown where applicable

Invoices that omit a valid PO number will be returned to the supplier. The payment clock does not start until a compliant invoice is re-submitted.

4. EARLY PAYMENT DISCOUNTS

Suppliers may offer early payment discounts (dynamic discounting). Proposals must be submitted to the Accounts Payable team and, if accepted, documented as a formal amendment to the relevant contract. The company does not operate a supply-chain finance programme at this time.

5. DISPUTED INVOICES

If an invoice is disputed, the Accounts Payable team must notify the supplier within five working days, specifying the nature of the dispute. The undisputed portion of the invoice will be paid on the standard payment schedule. The payment clock for the disputed portion is paused until the dispute is resolved.

6. LATE PAYMENT

If the company fails to pay a valid invoice by the due date, statutory interest accrues at 8% above the Bank of England base rate, in accordance with the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998. The company aims to resolve any late-payment issues within five working days of identification.

7. POLICY REVIEW

This policy is reviewed annually by the Finance and Procurement Committee. The most recent substantive revision was made in response to the 2024 UK Procurement Act guidance. Note: this version is over six months old and should be re-verified against current legislative references before reliance.

title: Supplier Data Protection Requirements
content:
SUPPLIER DATA PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS

Version 3.0 | Legal & Compliance

1. PURPOSE AND LEGAL BASIS

This document sets out the minimum data protection and information security requirements that all suppliers must meet when processing personal data on behalf of the company. It supplements the standard Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and derives from the UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, and the company's Information Security Policy.

2. SCOPE

These requirements apply to any supplier that:
(a) processes personal data provided by or on behalf of the company;
(b) has access to systems or environments containing personal data; or
(c) provides services that involve generating, storing, or transmitting personal data relating to the company's employees, customers, or business contacts.

3. MANDATORY TECHNICAL MEASURES

3.1 Encryption: Personal data must be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher and at rest using AES-256 or equivalent. Suppliers must not transmit personal data over unencrypted channels.

3.2 Access Control: Access to personal data must be restricted to personnel who require it for the performance of contracted services (principle of least privilege). All access must be authenticated using multi-factor authentication (MFA) for remote access and for any privileged accounts.

3.3 Logging and Monitoring: Suppliers must maintain access logs for systems that hold personal data for a minimum of 12 months. Logs must be tamper-resistant and available for audit upon request.

3.4 Vulnerability Management: Suppliers must have a documented vulnerability management programme including regular patching (critical vulnerabilities patched within 72 hours of public disclosure) and periodic penetration testing (at least annually for Tier 1 suppliers).

4. INCIDENT REPORTING

Suppliers must notify the company's Data Protection Officer within 24 hours of becoming aware of a personal data breach that affects company data, regardless of severity. The initial notification must include the nature of the breach, estimated number of records affected, and immediate containment actions taken. A full incident report must follow within 72 hours.

5. SUBPROCESSORS

Suppliers may not engage subprocessors to process company personal data without prior written consent. A list of approved subprocessors must be maintained and shared with the company upon request. Any change to subprocessors requires 30 days' advance written notice.

6. DATA RETENTION AND DELETION

Upon termination or expiry of the contract, the supplier must securely delete or return all personal data within 30 days, and provide written confirmation of deletion. Media destruction must follow NIST 800-88 or equivalent standards.

7. AUDIT RIGHTS

The company reserves the right to audit supplier compliance with these requirements upon 14 days' written notice, or immediately in the event of a suspected breach. Suppliers must cooperate fully and provide access to relevant systems, documentation, and personnel.

title: Sanctions and Restricted Party Screening
content:
SANCTIONS AND RESTRICTED PARTY SCREENING POLICY

Version 2.4 | Legal & Compliance

1. PURPOSE

This policy establishes the mandatory screening requirements to ensure the company does not engage in commercial relationships with individuals, entities, or jurisdictions subject to applicable sanctions or export control regimes. Compliance with sanctions law is a legal obligation and non-compliance may expose the company and individual employees to criminal liability.

2. APPLICABLE REGIMES

Screening must be performed against, at minimum, the following lists:
- UK HM Treasury Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation (OFSI) Consolidated List
- EU Consolidated List of Persons, Groups and Entities subject to EU financial sanctions
- US Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List
- US Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) Entity List
- UN Security Council Consolidated List

The Legal and Compliance team maintains a current register of applicable regimes and updates it within five business days of any material regulatory change.

3. SCREENING REQUIREMENTS

3.1 All new suppliers must be screened prior to onboarding. See Supplier Onboarding Policy for workflow integration.
3.2 All existing suppliers on the Approved Supplier List must be re-screened at least annually and upon any change of ownership or key personnel.
3.3 Screening must include the supplier's legal entity name, trading names, ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs), directors, and any entity holding more than 25% ownership.
3.4 For suppliers operating in or from high-risk jurisdictions (as published by OFSI, OFAC, or the Financial Action Task Force), enhanced due diligence must be performed regardless of the screening result.

4. SCREENING TOOLS

The company uses [screening platform] as its primary screening tool. Manual screening against published government lists is an acceptable fallback in the event of system outage, documented in the Procurement team's business continuity plan.

5. MATCH HANDLING

5.1 A potential match is any result returned by the screening tool with a match confidence above the configured threshold.
5.2 All potential matches must be reviewed by a member of the Legal and Compliance team within two business days.
5.3 A confirmed match results in immediate suspension of the commercial relationship and notification to the CFO and Company Secretary. Engagement with the supplier must cease pending legal advice.
5.4 A false positive must be documented with a written rationale and approved by the Head of Legal before onboarding or continued engagement proceeds.

6. RECORD-KEEPING

Screening results, including false positive determinations, must be retained for a minimum of seven years and are subject to regulatory audit.

7. TRAINING

All procurement and finance staff with supplier approval authority must complete sanctions compliance training annually. New starters must complete training within 30 days of joining.

title: Supplier Risk Tiering Guide
content:
SUPPLIER RISK TIERING GUIDE

Version 1.8 | Procurement Policy Office

1. PURPOSE

This guide defines the criteria for assigning a Risk Tier to each supplier on the Approved Supplier List (ASL). The Risk Tier drives the level of due diligence, approval authority, contract terms, and ongoing monitoring applied to the relationship.

2. TIER DEFINITIONS

Tier 1 — Strategic and Critical Suppliers
A supplier is classified as Tier 1 if it meets any of the following criteria:
- Annual spend exceeds £500,000
- The supplier is the sole or primary source for a product or service with no viable alternative within 90 days
- Disruption to the supplier's service would materially impact revenue, regulatory compliance, or customer commitments
- The supplier processes sensitive personal data (special category data under UK GDPR) on behalf of the company

Tier 1 suppliers require executive (CEO or CFO) sign-off for initial onboarding and annual review by the Procurement Committee.

Tier 2 — Significant Suppliers
A supplier is classified as Tier 2 if it meets any of the following criteria:
- Annual spend is between £50,000 and £500,000
- The supplier provides services that, if disrupted, would cause meaningful operational inconvenience but with a viable workaround within 30 days
- The supplier holds confidential company information (non-personal) under a non-disclosure agreement

Tier 2 suppliers require Head of Procurement sign-off and are reviewed every two years or at contract renewal.

Tier 3 — Standard Suppliers
All other approved suppliers. Tier 3 suppliers are subject to standard onboarding checks and are reviewed every three years.

3. TIERING PROCESS

3.1 The Onboarding Lead assigns a provisional tier at the point of onboarding based on the information in the Supplier Nomination Form.
3.2 The provisional tier is confirmed or adjusted following receipt of due diligence documents.
3.3 Tier can be escalated (but not de-escalated without sign-off from the Head of Procurement) at any point during the relationship if circumstances change.

4. MONITORING REQUIREMENTS BY TIER

| Requirement | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sanctions re-screen | Every 6 months | Annually | Annually |
| Financial health check | Annually | At renewal | At renewal |
| Insurance certificate renewal | Annually | At renewal | At renewal |
| Performance review | Quarterly | Annually | At renewal |
| Contingency plan required | Yes | Recommended | No |

5. ESCALATION TRIGGERS

Any of the following events must trigger an immediate tier review:
- Supplier enters administration, receivership, or equivalent insolvency proceedings
- A sanctions screening match is returned (see Sanctions and Restricted Party Screening Policy)
- A material data or security incident involving the supplier
- A change of ownership or corporate restructuring affecting the supplier
- Persistent poor performance over two consecutive review periods

title: Insurance and Liability Requirements
content:
INSURANCE AND LIABILITY REQUIREMENTS FOR SUPPLIERS

Version 2.0 | Finance & Procurement

1. PURPOSE

This document sets out the minimum insurance coverage that suppliers must maintain throughout the duration of any contract with the company. Adequate insurance protects both the supplier and the company against financial loss arising from incidents, negligence, or unforeseen events during the performance of the contract.

2. MANDATORY INSURANCE TYPES

2.1 Employers' Liability Insurance
All suppliers that employ staff in the United Kingdom must hold Employers' Liability insurance with a minimum limit of £5,000,000 per occurrence, as required by the Employers' Liability (Compulsory Insurance) Act 1969.

2.2 Public Liability Insurance
Suppliers providing services on company premises or in the presence of company employees must hold Public Liability insurance with a minimum limit of £2,000,000 per occurrence (£5,000,000 for Tier 1 suppliers as defined in the Supplier Risk Tiering Guide).

2.3 Professional Indemnity Insurance
Suppliers providing professional, advisory, design, or technology services must hold Professional Indemnity (PI) insurance. Minimum limits:
- Tier 3 suppliers: £500,000 per claim
- Tier 2 suppliers: £1,000,000 per claim
- Tier 1 suppliers: £5,000,000 per claim, or the contract value, whichever is greater

2.4 Cyber Liability Insurance
Suppliers that process, store, or transmit company data (including personal data) must hold Cyber Liability insurance with a minimum limit of £1,000,000 per incident. This requirement applies regardless of Risk Tier.

3. EVIDENCE OF COVERAGE

Suppliers must provide a certificate of insurance naming the company as an additional insured (where permissible by the insurer) prior to contract commencement. Certificates must be renewed and re-submitted to Procurement within 10 business days of the policy renewal date. Failure to maintain required coverage is a material breach of contract.

4. SUBCONTRACTORS

Prime contractors are responsible for ensuring that any subcontractors engaged on company-related work maintain equivalent levels of insurance. Evidence of subcontractor insurance must be available upon request.

5. WAIVER PROCESS

A supplier that cannot meet specific coverage requirements may request a formal waiver. Waiver requests must be submitted in writing to the Head of Procurement and approved by the CFO. Waivers are granted on a case-by-case basis and documented in the contract record.

6. REVIEW NOTE

This policy was last reviewed in Version 2.0. Insurance market conditions and minimum limits should be validated against current market practice before use. The Finance team should confirm whether the cyber liability threshold remains appropriate given recent industry guidance. This document may be out of date with respect to current minimum coverage thresholds.

title: Quality Certification Requirements
content:
QUALITY CERTIFICATION REQUIREMENTS FOR SUPPLIERS

Version 1.5 | Quality Assurance Office

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE

This policy defines the quality certifications and standards that suppliers must hold when providing goods or services in categories where quality assurance is a critical requirement. It applies to all suppliers on the Approved Supplier List (ASL) whose supply category is flagged as quality-critical during onboarding.

2. CERTIFICATION CATEGORIES

2.1 Manufacturing and Physical Goods Suppliers
Suppliers providing physical goods for incorporation into company products or delivered to customers must hold ISO 9001:2015 (Quality Management Systems) certification from an accredited certification body. Equivalents recognised under the International Accreditation Forum (IAF) multilateral agreement are acceptable.

2.2 IT and Software Development Suppliers
Suppliers providing software development, managed IT services, or cloud infrastructure must demonstrate compliance with ISO/IEC 27001:2022 (Information Security Management). Where the supplier also processes personal data, ISO 27701 certification or an equivalent privacy management framework is strongly recommended.

2.3 Environmental Services Suppliers
Suppliers providing facilities management, waste management, or environmental services must hold ISO 14001:2015 (Environmental Management Systems) certification or demonstrate equivalent compliance with the company's Environmental and Sustainability Policy.

2.4 Professional Services Suppliers
For consulting, legal, financial advisory, and other professional services, formal ISO certification is not required. Instead, suppliers must demonstrate membership of the relevant professional regulatory body (e.g., FCA authorisation for financial services, SRA membership for legal services) and carry appropriate Professional Indemnity insurance as described in the Insurance and Liability Requirements Policy.

3. VERIFICATION

Certification documents must be submitted during onboarding and re-submitted upon expiry. The Quality Assurance Office verifies certificates directly with the issuing certification body where practicable. Expired certificates must be renewed and evidence of renewal submitted within 30 days of expiry. An expired certificate results in the supplier being placed in 'monitoring status' on the ASL; new purchase orders are not raised against monitoring-status suppliers.

4. CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT

Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers in quality-critical categories are expected to provide an annual quality report summarising:
- Non-conformances raised and resolved during the period
- Results of internal and external audits
- Corrective and preventive actions taken
- Any planned changes to quality management processes

5. NON-CONFORMANCE PROCESS

Where a supplier delivers goods or services that do not meet agreed quality standards, the relevant business unit raises a Non-Conformance Report (NCR) through the procurement system. The supplier must respond with a root cause analysis within five business days and a corrective action plan within 15 business days. Repeated non-conformances (three or more in a rolling 12-month period) trigger an escalated review under the Supplier Risk Tiering Guide.

title: Onboarding Brief Template
content:
SUPPLIER ONBOARDING BRIEF — TEMPLATE

Version 1.1 | Procurement Policy Office

INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE
This template is completed by the Onboarding Lead at the start of each new supplier onboarding engagement. It consolidates key information from the Supplier Nomination Form and due diligence documents into a single summary for sign-off. Complete all sections before presenting to the approving authority. Sections marked [REQUIRED] must not be left blank.

---

SECTION A — SUPPLIER IDENTIFICATION [REQUIRED]

Trading name (if different): _______________
Registered company number: _______________
Country of incorporation: _______________

Primary procurement contact name: _______________

---

SECTION B — COMMERCIAL SUMMARY [REQUIRED]

Procuring business unit: _______________
Supply category: _______________
Estimated annual spend: £_______________
Proposed contract start date: _______________
Proposed contract duration: _______________

Basis for tier assignment (reference specific criteria from Supplier Risk Tiering Guide): _______________

SECTION D — COMPLIANCE CHECKLIST [REQUIRED]

Complete each item before presenting for sign-off:
